[[File:Serena Williams Australian Open 2009 5.jpg|thumb|upright=.8|[[Serena Williams career statistics#Tier I / Premier Mandatory & Premier 5 finals|Serena Williams]] has won a record 23 WTA 1000 singles titles.]]

[[WTA 1000 tournaments|WTA 1000]] is a category of [[tennis]] tournaments on the [[WTA Tour]] organized by the [[Women's Tennis Association]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Futterman |first=Matthew |date=2024-12-11 |title=How tennis players are ranked on the ATP and WTA Tour, and what rankings mean for tournaments |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5847687/2024/12/10/tennis-rankings-how-players-ranked-atp-wta-explained/ |access-date=2025-07-14 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

The Series was initially called [[WTA Tier I tournaments|WTA Tier I]] which began in [[1988 WTA Tour|1988]] and lasted until [[2008 WTA Tour|2008]]. Records before [[1990 WTA Tour|1990]] are excluded from this list.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tandon |first=Kamakshi |date=2008-10-29 |title=Tandon: Ten notable features of the Roadmap |url=https://www.espn.com/sports/tennis/columns/story?columnist=kamakshi_tandon&id=3670301 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160915042421/https://www.espn.com/sports/tennis/columns/story?columnist=kamakshi_tandon&id=3670301 |archive-date=15 September 2016 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> When the WTA Tour was established in 1990 there were initially six [[WTA Tier I tournaments|Tier I]] tournaments held annually in the first three years. The list thereafter expanded to eight events in [[1993 WTA Tour|1993]], nine in [[1997 WTA Tour|1997]] and ten in [[2004 WTA Tour|2004]], before being scaled back to nine for [[2008 WTA Tour|2008]].

In [[2009 WTA Tour|2009]] the WTA changed the tournament categories, so that the majority of Tier I and [[WTA Tier II tournaments|Tier II]] tournaments were in one category, [[WTA Premier Tournaments|Premier Tournaments]], split into three categories: two of them being [[WTA Premier tournaments|Premier Mandatory and Premier 5]], comprising nine events being held with Wuhan, which replaced [[Pan Pacific Open|Tokyo]] in [[2014 WTA Tour|2014]], as the only exception.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Toray Pan Pacific Open WTA 2023 |url=https://tennisuptodate.com/pan-pacific-open |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230928122545/https://tennisuptodate.com/pan-pacific-open |archive-date=28 Sep 2023 |access-date=2023-09-28 |website=tennisuptodate.com}}</ref>

[[WTA Premier tournaments|WTA Premier]] Mandatory and Premier 5 tournaments merged into a single highest tier and it is implemented since the reorganization of the schedule in [[2021 WTA Tour|2021]].<ref name="wta">{{Cite web |date=2 December 2020 |title=WTA unveils comprehensive rebrand |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/1922290/wta-unveils-comprehensive-rebrand |website=WTA Tour |publisher=Women's Tennis Association (WTA)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2 December 2020 |title=WTA will align tournament categories with ATP from 2021 season |url=https://www.skysports.com/tennis/news/12110/12148935/wta-will-align-tournament-categories-with-atp-from-2021-season |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220926131953/https://www.skysports.com/tennis/news/12110/12148935/wta-will-align-tournament-categories-with-atp-from-2021-season |archive-date=26 September 2022 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref>

In [[2024 WTA Tour|2024]] the WTA expanded to ten WTA 1000 tournaments, up from nine in [[2023 WTA Tour|2023]], with both [[WTA Qatar Open|Doha]] and [[Dubai Tennis Championships|Dubai]] becoming 1000 events every year instead of alternating.<ref name="24mod">{{Cite web |date=14 January 2024 |title=WTA confirms 2024 calendar with increase in prize money for players |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/3856904/wta-confirms-2024-calendar-with-increase-in-prize-money-for-players |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240115153801/https://www.wtatennis.com/news/3856904/wta-confirms-2024-calendar-with-increase-in-prize-money-for-players |archive-date=January 15, 2024 |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=Women's Tennis Association |language=en }}</ref> There are ten WTA 1000 tournaments: [[WTA Qatar Open|Doha]], [[Dubai Tennis Championships|Dubai]], [[Indian Wells Masters|Indian Wells]], [[Miami Open (tennis)|Miami]], [[Madrid Open (tennis)|Madrid]], [[Italian Open (tennis)|Rome]], [[Canadian Open (tennis)|Canada]], [[Cincinnati Masters|Cincinnati]], [[China Open (tennis)|Beijing]] and [[Wuhan Open|Wuhan]].<ref name="2024cal">{{Cite web |title=2024 WTA Tour Calendar |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/tournaments/2024 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128211334/https://www.wtatennis.com/tournaments/2024 |archive-date=28 November 2023 |publisher=Women's Tennis Association}}</ref>

These tournaments offer 1000 ranking points for the winner.<ref name="24mod" />

Only [[:Category:Tennis events cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic|three tournaments]] were held in [[2020 WTA Tour|2020]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]: Doha, Rome and Cincinnati.<ref name="suspension3">{{Cite web |date=15 May 2020 |title=WTA announces further suspension of four tournaments |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/1669332/wta-announces-further-suspension-of-four-tournaments |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200602052700/https://www.wtatennis.com/news/1669332/wta-announces-further-suspension-of-four-tournaments |archive-date=2 June 2020 |website=WTA Tennis}}</ref><ref name="china swing">{{Cite web |date=24 July 2020 |title=WTA tournaments in China cancelled for 2020 |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/1738145/wta-tournaments-in-china-cancelled-for-2020 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301035712/https://www.wtatennis.com/news/1738145/wta-tournaments-in-china-cancelled-for-2020 |archive-date=1 March 2021 |publisher=WTA}}</ref>

[[Guadalajara Open Akron|Guadalajara]] replaced Wuhan and Beijing in [[2022 WTA Tour|2022]] due to the [[disappearance of Peng Shuai]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shyam Kamal |date=9 December 2021 |title=Peng Shuai: Everything you need to know about the saga – A complete timeline of events |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/tennis/everything-need-know-peng-shuai-saga-complete-timeline-events |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201232543/https://www.sportskeeda.com/tennis/everything-need-know-peng-shuai-saga-complete-timeline-events |archive-date=1 December 2022 |website=sportskeeda}}</ref><ref name="peng1">{{Cite web |date=2021-07-01 |title=WTA officially cancels 2021 fall Asian swing |url=http://opencourt.ca/2021/07/01/wta-officially-cancels-2021-fall-asian-swing/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20220924165036/https://opencourt.ca/2021/07/01/wta-officially-cancels-2021-fall-asian-swing/ |archive-date=2022-09-24 |website=Open Court}}</ref>

On 1 March 2022, the [[Women's Tennis Association|WTA]] announced that players from [[Belarus]] will not be allowed to compete under the name or flag of Belarus following the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 March 2022 |title=Joint Statement by the International Governing Bodies of Tennis |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/news/2510418/joint-statement-by-the-international-governing-bodies-of-tennis |access-date=29 December 2022 |website=WTA Tour}}</ref>
